standard_prerequisites.name: The group of $k$-cycles as the free abelian group on integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, the definition of the group $Z_k(X)$ (used at proof lines 1982-1984)
standard_prerequisites.use: In the quasi-compact case it turns the question into a statement about free modules on the integral closed subschemes $Z \subset X$ of $\delta$-dimension $k$, so exactness can be read off from bases.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pushforward of cycles along a closed immersion and the scheme theoretic intersection
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, the pushforward of cycles along closed immersions (statement lines 1977-1978, used at proof lines 1985-1986)
standard_prerequisites.use: They give the maps in the sequence and identify $Z_k(X_1)$, $Z_k(X_2)$, $Z_k(X_1 \cap X_2)$ with the free subgroups spanned by those basis elements contained in $X_1$, in $X_2$, or in the scheme theoretic intersection.

core_obligations: Reduce to the case where $X$ is quasi-compact, the general case being analogous (proof lines 1982 and 1987-1988).

Identify $Z_k(X)$ with the free abelian group on the integral closed subschemes of $\delta$-dimension $k$, and the three other groups with the free subgroups obtained by restricting the containment to $X_1$, to $X_2$ and to $X_1 \cap X_2$ (proof lines 1982-1986).
Read off surjectivity of the last map and exactness at the middle term from these bases, the maps being the pushforwards with one sign changed (proof lines 1986-1988).
proof_roadmap: Free bases and the subgroups they span (proof lines 1982-1986).
Exactness from the basis description (proof lines 1986-1988).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives right exactness of the sequence of cycle groups attached to a cover of $X$ by two closed subschemes, at the level of the groups $Z_k$ before passing to rational equivalence (statement lines 1963-1979). The proof is carried out in the quasi-compact case by choosing the free basis of integral closed subschemes and identifying the subgroups spanned by those contained in each piece; the general case is stated to be analogous. The basis analysis is the substance, so the claim is H2.
